title: Users and groups
subtitle: passwd, shadow, su/sudo, and account tools — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.notes: Kernel cares about UID/GID numbers, not the pretty name. Expiration is not on this line.

cards.meaning: Hash lives in /etc/shadow (root-only), not in world-readable passwd
cards.notes: Stops ordinary users from copying hashes out of passwd and cracking them.

cards.meaning: Password hash, lock markers, aging, and account expiration
cards.notes: Secret and time. Memory hook: passwd = who; shadow = secret and time.
Prefer sudo for one command. Do not use root without necessity. Low UIDs are often system accounts.

cards.meaning: Primary = GID in passwd; supplementary = member list in /etc/group
cards.notes: Empty /etc/group member list ≠ unused group — users can still have that GID as primary.
Group password is rare (empty or x). Primary membership is on the user line, not always here.

cards.meaning: Substitute user — needs the target user’s password (except root switching down)
cards.notes: su - = full login (home + profile). su user keeps more of your environment. su alone → root.

cards.meaning: Run a command with another user’s privileges (usually root); asks for YOUR password if allowed
cards.notes: sudo = your password (via sudoers). su = target password. sudo su ≈ root shell without knowing root’s secret.

cards.meaning: Create a user with home directory and login shell
Delete the account and remove home/files
cards.notes: userdel without -r leaves the home directory behind.

cards.meaning: Append a supplementary group; without -a, -G replaces the extra-group set
cards.notes: gpasswd -a user group does the same idea. Renaming with usermod -l does not change UID or file ownership.

cards.meaning: Set or change a password hash in shadow
cards.notes: Root can passwd otheruser without the old password. * or ! in shadow locks password login.

cards.meaning: Show password aging and account expiry from shadow
cards.notes: usermod -e YYYY-MM-DD sets account expiration. After expiry, login is refused even with a correct password.

cards.meaning: Account exists for daemons/files but must not get a login shell
cards.notes: Login shell is what starts at interactive login; user can still type bash after they are in if they somehow get a shell.

cards.meaning: Create, delete, or rename/change a group
cards.notes: Rename keeps the same GID — existing files still show the new name. groups lists membership by name.

cards.meaning: Print UID, primary GID, and all groups for the process
cards.notes: id -u numeric UID; id -g primary GID; id -G all GIDs. Two passwd lines with the same UID are the same identity to the kernel.
